argument: The only cost in the statement rises with temperature, which the fixed table decides does not carry resistance, and the cap is set by the second law, not by any resistance quantity; an inequality is not an equivalence, so no rule-compliant turn exists.

The relation is a definition whose variables (enthalpy, internal energy, pressure, volume) are all fixed as not carrying resistance, and no cost or distance-made separation appears in the statement; definitions keep their shape, so no rule-compliant turn exists.
This is a conservation law, which the rule says keeps its shape; no variable carries resistance and no cost is present, so there is nothing for the mirror to turn.

The strongest keeps reading would rest on the parenthetical definition of thermal resistance (thickness over conductivity times area), but the statement's core is a cost caused by thermal resistance, which the fixed table marks as carrying resistance, and the rule turns such a cost around; the embedded definition of the resistance cannot keep the whole relation while the cost it causes turns, so no rule-compliant keeps reading exists.

The relation is a definition with no costs, and free energy, enthalpy, temperature and entropy are all fixed as not carrying resistance; definitions keep their shape, so no rule-compliant turn exists.

The statement is a definition, and heat capacity's carrying of resistance is fixed as UNDETERMINED, so no turn may rest on the thermal-inertia reading; with no decided resistance quantity and no cost in the statement, the definition keeps its shape and no rule-compliant turn exists.

The strongest keeps reading would treat P = I² × R as a bare proportionality, but the statement's cost (energy lost to heat) rises with electrical resistance, which the fixed table marks as carrying resistance, and the rule turns resistance-caused costs around; the statement contains no equivalence, definition or conservation to keep, so no rule-compliant keeps reading exists.

The strongest keeps reading would call the heat taken a mere scaling with how much body there is, but the fixed table decides mass m as carrying resistance and flags latent heat's rise with mass as exactly this relation-level cost; Q = m × L is a proportionality, not an equivalence or definition, so no rule-compliant keeps reading exists.
The relation is a definition, and latent heat and heat are fixed as not carrying resistance; definitions keep their shape, so no rule-compliant turn exists.

The cost rises with entropy, which the fixed table decides does not carry resistance, and the Kelvin-Planck limit is caused by heat, not by any resistance quantity; no equivalence appears in the statement, so no rule-compliant turn exists.
The relation is an identity, which keeps its shape; although mass m carries resistance, no cost or limit caused by it appears in the statement, so there is nothing to turn.

The statement is an evening-out with no cost, and temperature and heat are both fixed as not carrying resistance; the equalizing approach behaves like a symmetry, which keeps its shape, so no rule-compliant turn exists.

The cost rises with temperature, fixed as not carrying resistance, and the unreachability of the zero is caused by each step removing a smaller fraction, not by any resistance quantity; the limit is therefore not a resistance-caused limit, so no rule-compliant turn exists.
The relation is a definition of what makes temperature well-defined, with no cost and no resistance-carrying quantity; definitions keep their shape, so no rule-compliant turn exists.
